title: Mood never costs clear words
statement: Direct a narration voice so its mood never costs intelligibility: no exaggerated delivery that obscures the words, no flat list reading and no tone younger than the learners.
detail: The handover's direction for a narrated opening asks for an epic, atmospheric, theatrical and ominous voice that never becomes exaggerated, melodramatic or difficult to understand, while preserving clear words. It names the deliveries to avoid: an exaggerated trailer voice that obscures meaning, robotic list delivery and childish enthusiasm. The prototype's narration handoff asks for one grounded storyteller, steady and clear.
against: Direction did not settle the right pace for older learners or how old a voice sounds: "Gacrux on gemini-2.5-pro reads this script at about 140 words a minute in any direction, which cannot fit three minutes without stretching." (`g9/film/v07/README.md`, lines 17-18). The film then took a brisker take, "2:54 at 158 words a minute: a new brisk take, no words cut, no time-stretch" (the same file, line 10), and in blind judging "on scene 4 two of three preferred the brisker read, and one heard it as "far too young"" (lines 19-20).

evidence.quote: The voice should be epic, atmospheric, theatrical, and ominous without becoming exaggerated, melodramatic, or difficult to understand.
Ask for epic scale, atmosphere, theatrical intention, and ominous gravity while preserving clear words and a measured pace.
Avoid an exaggerated trailer voice that obscures meaning, robotic list delivery, childish enthusiasm, or an actor imitation.
Voice direction: one grounded storyteller, steady and clear.
